text: Hello everyone, welcome to my class.In the previous lessons, we finished section A, reading and interaction.Today, we are going to start section B, grammar activity, the unreal conditional.By the end of this period, you are expected to identify the different forms of the unreal conditional and their meanings in the given context.You are also expected to use the unreal conditional correctly in different contexts.Before starting, please make sure your textbook and the worksheet are at hand.In the previous lessons, we learned about the advantages and disadvantages of immortality.What will we do if we accept that life is limited?Would you please answer this question in your own words?You will have 10 seconds.Time is up.Have you got the answer?If we accept that life is limited, we will cherish time more.Yes, since life is limited, we need to cherish time and think about how to live a meaningful life.But for some people, it takes luck to simply survive.Now please open your textbook and turn to page 38.Today, we are going to read a passage about a man's lucky escapes and a lucky break.While reading, please find the answers to the following questions.You may underline the evidence in the passage, and you will have two minutes.Please find the answers to the following questions in the passage, and you will have two minutes.Let's check the answers.Question 1.Emma, what's your answer?Yes, I totally agree.If you were Frank, you'd be happy to be alive because he met with serious accidents in the 1960s, in the 1970s, and in 1994, he was lucky enough to survive them all.It's miraculous.Good.I've got the same feeling.If I were Frank, I would be happy to be alive.What about question 2?Leo, can you have a try?The people in the village saved him.If it hadn't been for the people in the village, Frank could have drowned.Well done.Frank survived the accident because of the people in the village.If they hadn't saved him, he could have died.Then, question 3.Lily, what's your answer?It was his luck.If Frank's luck had run out, this would be the end of his story.So Frank was quite lucky.If his luck had run out, he could have died.The last one, Henry.No, it's not because he gave all the money away.If Frank were a greedy man, he would have kept the money for himself.Excellent.So if Frank were a greedy man is an assumption.In fact, he is not greedy at all.Now please look at these five sentences.What do they have in common?Yes, all of them are conditionals.But there are also differences among them.We will compare these sentences and try to find out their differences.Now, let's focus on these three sentences.And please answer the following questions.Let's look at these sentences.Sentence 1 is about the present real situation.In this sentence, the if clause, if we accept that life is limited, is about the present real situation.And the main clause, we will cherish time more, is about the possible future result.The verb accept in the if clause is in the present simple.Sentence 2 is about the present unreal situation.If you were Frank, is the unreal situation because it is impossible for you to become him.The verb were in the if clause is in the past simple.Sentence 3 is about the past unreal situation.If it hadn't been for the people in the village, is the unreal situation.Frank didn't drown because the people in the village helped him.The verb hadn't been in the if clause is in the past perfect.In fact, there are three common types of conditional clauses for expressing real or unreal conditions in the present or in the past.They are the first conditional, the second conditional, and the third conditional.The first conditional is used when we talk about a real or possible situation.Obviously, sentence 1 is the first conditional.The second conditional is used to talk about unreal situations at present or in the future.Which sentence is the second conditional?Yes, it's sentence 2.The third conditional is used to talk about unreal situations in the past.So sentence 3 is the third conditional.I think you are quite familiar with the first conditional.Today, our focus is the unreal conditional.Now, let's study the structure of the second conditional.The verb in the if clause is in the simple past tense and would plus bare infinitive in the main clause in this structure.After I or he or she or it, we often use the verb form were, not was.I'll give you another example.If I were you, I would be careful about sharing personal information online.Let's look at sentence 3.What is the structure of the third conditional?Can you work it out?Yes, the verb in the if clause is in the past perfect tense and could have plus past participle in the main clause.In fact, besides would, modal verbs such as could and might can also be used in the main clauses of the second and the third conditionals.Here is an example.If Johnsey hadn't seen the last firm ivy leaf, he might not have had the courage to fight against pneumonia.Are you clear about the structures of the second and the third conditionals?Now, let's look at the last two sentences.Pay attention to the verbs in the if clauses and the main clauses.Do they follow the structures of the second or the third conditional?The conditional clause is if Frank's luck had run out.The main clause is this would be the end of his story.The verb in the if clause is in the past perfect tense, but the verb in the main clause is would plus bare infinitive.So this conditional combines a past condition with a present result.Can you analyze the structure of sentence five?In sentence five, the conditional clause is if Frank were a greedy man.The main clause is he would have kept the money for himself.The verb in the if clause is in the simple past tense, but the verb in the main clause is would have plus past participle.This conditional combines a present condition with a past result.These conditionals are called mixed conditionals.As you can see, they are a mixture of the second and the third conditionals.These are the rules about the unreal conditional you have just learned.You will have the next 20 seconds to review them.If we want to express possible results of unreal situations, we can use the unreal conditional.Now can you match the first part of a conditional sentence with its logical mate?You will have 30 seconds to do the match work.Have you got the answers?Number one, if I won the lottery, I would donate the money to our local hospital.Number two, if I had traveled on that train, I would have been hurt in the accident.Number three, if it hadn't been for your timely help, I wouldn't be here safe and sound.Number four, if I were a doctor, I would have saved the victim at that time.Good job!Let's analyze these sentences.The first one is a second conditional.We use it to imagine and to dream that the present situation is different from what it really is.It's unlikely that I will win the lottery.Possible, but unlikely.So, donating the money to the local hospital is an unlikely event.Who can analyze the rest of the sentences?Number two is a third conditional.I was not hurt because I didn't travel on that train.I think the speaker was quite lucky.Number three is a mixed conditional.Because of your timely help, I am safe and sound now.This sentence shows the speaker is very grateful.Number four is also a mixed conditional.I am not a doctor, so I didn't manage to save the victim at that time.It shows the speaker's regret.You've explained their meanings clearly.Do you remember, after many lucky escapes, Frank finally had his first lucky break and won a million dollars on the national lottery?This time, we are going to read a story about a woman who won an even bigger fortune through the lottery.Complete the passage with the correct form of the words in brackets.You will have two minutes for that.Number one, would it really make?If you suddenly won the lottery is the unreal condition.Number two, went.If you went to your local supermarket is an imaginary situation.Number one and number two both talk about the present situations.Number three, had known.She was not likely to know what would happen to her after she won the lottery.Number three is about an unreal past situation.Number four hadn't been.Because she received the money.She is not working as a shop assistant now.Number five wouldn't be.She chose the winning numbers.So her life is different now.She's lucky.Number six would be.They actually won the lottery.But their lives now are not as good as they thought.They feel regretful for being lottery winners.Number four to number six talk about past conditions with present results.People have different definitions of luck.They have different feelings when they win the lottery.The unreal conditional can be used to express such feelings.For example, when winning the lottery.King feels lucky.While some other winners claim that their lives would be much better today.If they hadn't won the lottery.But if King hadn't used her money wisely.How would she feel now?Now can you think of a reason to regret that you have?Is there anything that you did or didn't do and now feel regretful about?Write it using this pattern.You may use the example below to help you.You will have 30 seconds to prepare.Who would like to share Oliver?I have one big regret.Yesterday, I didn't pay attention in class.So now I don't know how to do the assignment.If I had paid more attention in class.I wouldn't be struggling with the assignment now.Oliver, what would you do if you were given a second chance?If there was such an opportunity.I will listen attentively in class and write down all the requirements of the assignment.Good, you've already learned from your mistake.I think you must have more to share.Now ask at least three classmates about their regrets.Select the biggest regret to report to the class.When you talk, please try to use the unreal conditional as much as you can.You will have two minutes for the task.Let's hear your report.I think the biggest regret is James.He said I was hurt when I fell off the bicycle last Sunday.If I had worn my bicycle helmet, I wouldn't have been hurt.I didn't tell my parents how I got hurt.If my father had found out I rode a bicycle without a helmet, he would have scolded me.If my mother had known that, she would have been very worried.In a word, if I were given a second chance, I would definitely wear my helmet when riding a bicycle.So James' regret is that he didn't follow the safety rules of cycling.We can't go back and change what happened in the past.Can we?What we should do is learn to deal with feelings of regret by reflecting on them, learning from mistakes, and then letting go.Here comes today's homework.Thanks for watching.See you next time.
